correctness.rationale: For n=3,5,7, the nonlinear centered maximal norm is exactly the maximum squared singular norm over all legal ball-selection matrices. Exact integer Sylvester elimination in the included verifier covers 18, 1200, and 176400 selections, excluding all but 1, 2, and 1 exceptional cases at strict rational thresholds. Exact characteristic identities, trace bounds, rational Rayleigh witnesses, rational root brackets, positive eigenvectors with polynomial residual identities, irreducibility, and strict averaging inequalities prove the stated constants, attainment, and complete extremizer classification. The numerical approximations are not used as proof; no infinite-n extrapolation is claimed.

value.rationale: Odd paths are canonical discrete one-dimensional domains with a naturally distinguished center. Exact sharp strong Hilbert constants and full extremizer rays on P5 and P7 show that the largest extremizer coordinate unexpectedly moves away from the center at P5 but returns uniquely to the center at P7, despite the unchanged class of centered graph-ball averaging. This re-entrant localization is a motivated finite boundary rather than a routine isolated constant, and is a concrete equality-case benchmark for studying paths. The theorem does not assert a general odd-path pattern.
